properties.name: stx.errors.enabled
properties.description: Register the stx error handling. Off unless set: putting this library on the classpath must not change how an application already reports failures.

properties.name: stx.errors.include-debug-message
properties.description: Serialize ApiException.debugMessage into the response. Leave off outside development: a debug message is routinely a query, a constraint name or an upstream body.

properties.name: stx.security.enabled
properties.description: Register the stx security beans: a BCrypt PasswordEncoder and the meta-annotation template support that @RequireRole needs. Not a filter chain — which paths are open stays the application's decision.

properties.name: stx.security.bcrypt-strength
properties.description: The BCrypt work factor. Each step doubles the cost to hash and to attack. Raising it does not invalidate existing hashes: the cost is stored in the hash.

properties.name: stx.cors.enabled
properties.description: Register the CORS filter built from these properties.

properties.name: stx.cors.origins
properties.description: The exact origins allowed. Empty by default: a browser policy that arrives already permitting somebody is the wrong shape of default.

properties.name: stx.cors.origin-patterns
properties.description: Origins matched as patterns, so one entry covers every subdomain. The one that works with allow-credentials, because the concrete requesting origin is echoed back rather than a wildcard.

properties.name: stx.cors.methods
properties.description: The HTTP methods those origins may use.

properties.name: stx.cors.headers
properties.description: The request headers those origins may send.

properties.name: stx.cors.exposed-headers
properties.description: The response headers the browser is allowed to read. Empty means the CORS-safelisted ones.

properties.name: stx.cors.allow-credentials
properties.description: Whether the browser may send cookies and Authorization. Cannot be combined with an origins list of "*" — use origin-patterns.

properties.name: stx.cors.max-age
properties.description: How long a browser may cache the preflight answer, in seconds.

properties.name: stx.cors.path
properties.description: The path pattern this CORS configuration applies to.

properties.name: stx.json.enabled
properties.description: Make kotlinx-serialization the codec WebFlux reads and writes JSON with, in place of Jackson. Off because kotlinx serializes only what carries @Serializable, and switching a running application over is a decision rather than a detail.

properties.name: stx.json.explicit-nulls
properties.description: Whether a null property is written out at all. Off, so a response type with a dozen optional fields is not mostly nulls.

properties.name: stx.json.encode-defaults
properties.description: Whether a property equal to its default is written out. On, the opposite of the kotlinx default: a client that has never seen a field cannot know the default the server would have used.

properties.name: stx.data.mongo.enabled
properties.description: Register the stx Spring Data Mongo beans, starting with the kotlin.time.Instant converters. Separate from stx.mongo, which is the stx-mongo driver library's own integration.

properties.name: stx.data.mongo.gridfs-bucket
properties.description: The GridFS bucket a ReactiveGridFsTemplate is opened on. Unset means no template: a bucket that appears because nobody set a property is two collections in a database that never asked for them.

properties.name: stx.data.mongo.transactions
properties.description: Register a ReactiveMongoTransactionManager. Needs a replica set — a standalone mongod fails the first startTransaction rather than at startup.

properties.name: stx.data.mongo.auditor
properties.description: Register a ReactiveAuditorAware answering with the authenticated user's name, so @CreatedBy and @LastModifiedBy fill themselves in. Distinct from stx.data.mongo.audit, which keeps the document's whole history. Needs Spring Security, and @EnableReactiveMongoAuditing in the application.

properties.name: stx.data.mongo.create-indexes
properties.description: Create the indexes the mapped entities declare, once the application is ready. Nothing is ever dropped: rebuilding an index on a live collection means every query using it scans until it is done.

properties.name: stx.data.mongo.audit.enabled
properties.description: Record every save and delete of an @Auditable document as a version in a collection of its own. Off by default: an audit trail is a second copy of the data and a deployment's decision.

properties.name: stx.data.mongo.audit.collection
properties.description: The collection audit entries are written to. Changing it after entries exist starts a new, empty history.

properties.name: stx.mongo.enabled
properties.description: Open an stx-mongo coroutine client. Off by default. Distinct from stx.data.mongo and from Spring Boot's spring.data.mongodb, which configure Spring Data's ReactiveMongoTemplate — a different API onto the same server, and a second pool if both are on.

properties.name: stx.mongo.uri
properties.description: The connection string. Required when enabled: a default would be a guess about somebody's cluster.

properties.name: stx.mongo.database
properties.description: The database the MongoDatabase bean points at. Required when enabled.

properties.name: stx.i18n.enabled
properties.description: Load the message catalogs and narrow the locale resolver to the languages named below. Off by default.

properties.name: stx.i18n.languages
properties.description: The languages with catalogs — [en, fr], or [en, fr-CA] for a region. The version this replaces hardcoded en and fr in a @Configuration class.

properties.name: stx.i18n.fallback
properties.description: The language a key falls back to when the request's has no text for it. Per key, not per request.

properties.name: stx.i18n.base-name
properties.description: Where the .properties catalogs are — locales/messages_fr.properties for fr.

properties.name: stx.i18n.fail-on-missing-key
properties.description: Throw on a key with no text anywhere, instead of returning the key. Off in a deployment and worth turning on in a test suite: a running server should not fail a request over a translation, and a test suite should not pass over one.
